# Lab 19.8: Secure Agent Platform with VPC-SC & CMEK

## What We Are Going to Do
Encrypt an Agent Platform resource with your own key, then put the AI API inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter.

## Steps

1. **Enable the API and create a key in the same region.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com cloudkms.googleapis.com
export PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format="value(projectNumber)")
gcloud kms keyrings create ai-ring --location=us-central1
gcloud kms keys create ai-key --keyring=ai-ring --location=us-central1 --purpose=encryption</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Let the AI service agent use the key.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud beta services identity create --service=aiplatform.googleapis.com
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ai-key --keyring=ai-ring --location=us-central1 \
  --member=serviceAccount:service-$PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Create a CMEK-protected endpoint.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud ai endpoints create --region=us-central1 --display-name=cmek-endpoint \
  --encryption-kms-key-name=projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/keyRings/ai-ring/cryptoKeys/ai-key
gcloud ai endpoints list --region=us-central1 --format="table(displayName,encryptionSpec.kmsKeyName)"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **Call Gemini before the perimeter.** From Cloud Shell:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent" \
  -d '{"contents":[{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"Say hello"}]}]}' | head -20</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   It works. Use any Gemini model name currently available in your region.

5. **Add the AI API to the perimeter.** Using the perimeter from Lab 13.10, add the service in dry-run first, then enforce:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud access-context-manager perimeters dry-run update lab_perimeter \
  --add-restricted-services=aiplatform.googleapis.com --policy=$POLICY_ID
gcloud access-context-manager perimeters dry-run enforce lab_perimeter --policy=$POLICY_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **Test again.** Without an ingress rule for your identity, the same call returns `Request is prohibited by organization's policy`. Requests from inside the perimeter, for example a VM using `restricted.googleapis.com`, still work.

7. **Clean up.** Remove the service from the perimeter and delete the endpoint.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud ai endpoints delete ENDPOINT_ID --region=us-central1 --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | Encrypted with `ai-key` |
| Key region | Same as the AI resources |
| Outside calls | Blocked by the perimeter |
| Check first | Which AI features support CMEK and VPC-SC |
